title: Derived sections of complete reductions and the one-degree inverse-limit bound
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $B=\mathcal O_E$ with its norm topology, and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-étale site of any scheme $U$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], put $B_U=p_U^*C(-,B)$ and $k_{n,U}=(B/\pi^n)_U$ for $n\geq1$ [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Use ordinary uncompleted module-derived sections [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_U))$ be derived $\pi$-complete [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], and set
$$K_n=\operatorname{Res}_{B_U\to k_{n,U}}(K\otimes^L_{B_U}k_{n,U})$$
with the actual quotient transitions. Then the completion unit and derived limit comparison induce an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$
$$R\Gamma(U,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n R\Gamma(U,K_n).$$
Here $R\varprojlim$ is the strict-tower derived inverse limit, represented by the Roos fibre of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ [def-weil-derived-limit]. If an integer $h$ satisfies $H^qR\Gamma(U,K_n)=0$ for all $n\geq1$ and $q>h$, then $H^qR\Gamma(U,K)=0$ for every $q>h+1$. No surjectivity or Mittag--Leffler condition on cohomology transition maps is assumed. This includes $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $B=\mathbf Z_\ell$.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, for the derived sections/limit comparison; Bhatt--Scholze Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2 for the complete unit; Roos triangle in abelian groups for the upper bound.

proof.text: Apply the normalized resolution theorem to each K-flat representative. Completeness on that representative is invertibility of completionMap. Cancel its representative isomorphism to obtain invertibility of the specified augmentation, and apply the conditional conclusion of the normalized resolution. Functoriality of RΓ and c give the required invertible composite, with its normalization unchanged.

Choose the K-flat representative supplied by completeness and the comparison from the first clause. Its invertible composite gives an isomorphism from RΓ(K) to the section Roos fibre. Apply the Milnor sequence to that isomorphism.

If q>h+1 then q-1>h and q>h. The two cohomology towers in the Milnor sequence are zero objectwise, hence zero functors. The additive first right-derived inverse-limit functor preserves zero objects, and the limit cone of a zero diagram has zero vertex. Both end terms vanish; exactness forces the middle term to be zero. This argument treats all integer h and needs no Mittag--Leffler condition.

(5) The Milnor sequence holds for any countable tower in D(Ab). (6) Zero towers give lim = R^1 lim = 0, which is elementary.
